prediction.likelyOutcome: GF55 is likely to be found liable for negligent inspection/false Directive 14 certification given Gross's own trial admissions, with damages allocated partly to it and partly borne (nominally) by the defaulted, likely-judgment-proof JFB; the measurement claim is a closer call that could go either way given competing expert remeasurements that don't even agree on direction. Total recovery against GF55 on the quantified rent-overcharge theory alone is modest (roughly $10,000-$33,000), but the case's real value turns on the unpriced cost of remediating the code and construction deficiencies, which the inspection claim's strong liability picture would support if quantified.

issues.label: Negligent inspection / false Directive 14 certification claim
JFB Construction's defaulted liability for construction defects

outcome.description: After a two-day bench trial the court rejected Wax's lost-square-footage (rent overpayment) theory against GF55, finding no duty to measure for lease purposes and no proven deviation from the standard of care, but held GF55 liable for negligent TR1 inspections and awarded the remediation cost: $35,070 for black iron, $8,000 for fireproofing plus $10,000 protection and cleanup, and $1,177 for firestopping, a total of $54,247. The court separately entered a default judgment of $163,723 against the contractor JFB.
outcome.finalNote: No appeal reflected in the source. Amount verified ($54,247 against GF55 only); the $163,723 default judgment against JFB is excluded because the case valued is the contested claim against the architect. The remediation cost figures appear only in the damages findings, so the input has no dollar figure for the inspection claim; the calculator may decline or price only the rent theory.
